target: Il est resté chez lui toute la soirée.
english: He stayed home all evening.
tip: Chez plus a person means at their place: il est resté chez lui = he stayed at his home. There's no single English word for it.

target: Elle a gardé les enfants de sa voisine.
english: She watched her neighbor's children.
tip: Garder les enfants means to babysit, literally 'to keep the children': elle a gardé les enfants de sa voisine.

target: Elle a dit bonjour à tout le monde.
english: She said hello to everyone.
tip: "tout le monde" literally means "all the world," but it just means everyone: elle a dit bonjour à tout le monde = she said hi to everybody.

target: Tu as promené le chien ce matin ?
english: Did you walk the dog this morning?
tip: You 'walk' the dog with promener: tu as promené le chien. It means to take out for a walk – you're walking it, not strolling yourself.

target: Tu as fait les courses au supermarché ?
english: Did you do the shopping at the supermarket?
tip: "faire les courses" isn't running races – here courses means errands, and faire (to make/do) covers shopping: tu as fait les courses = did you do the shopping.

target: Elle a mis son manteau car il faisait froid.
english: She put on her coat because it was cold.
tip: French weather runs on 'faire': 'il faisait froid' is literally 'it was making cold'. Heat works the same way – 'il fait chaud'.

target: En fait, je préfère rester ici.
english: Actually, I prefer to stay here.
tip: 'En fait' means 'actually, in fact'. Don't reach for the false friend 'actuellement' – that one means 'currently'.

target: Elle est arrivée en retard au bureau.
english: She arrived late at the office.
tip: Verbs of motion use 'être' in passé composé: elle est arrivée. The past participle agrees with the subject (arrivée = feminine).

target: Elles ont ouvert les yeux très grand.
english: They opened their eyes very wide.
tip: French uses the plain article for body parts, not "their": elles ont ouvert les yeux = they opened the eyes, meaning their own. Ownership is understood.

target: Nous avons écrit à l'hôtel pour confirmer.
english: We wrote to the hotel to confirm.
tip: 'L'' replaces 'le/la' before vowels or silent 'h': 'l'hôtel', 'l'aéroport'. Mandatory elision.

target: Vraiment, je ne m'attendais pas à ce résultat.
english: Really, I didn't expect this result.
tip: 'S'attendre à' means to expect, not to wait – and it's reflexive with 'à': 'je ne m'attendais pas à ce résultat' = I didn't expect this.

target: Ils dinaient au restaurant quand la lumière s'est eteinte.
english: They were having dinner at the restaurant when the light went out.
tip: The imparfait sets the scene, the passé composé breaks it: 'dînaient' was the ongoing dinner, 's'est éteinte' the sudden moment the light died.

target: Partout dans la ville on entendait de la musique.
english: Everywhere in the city you could hear music.
tip: 'On' is the everyday stand-in for 'you/one/people in general': 'on entendait' = you could hear. It always takes the il/elle verb form.

target: Je cherchais un restaurant quand j'ai trouvé ce petit bistrot.
english: I was looking for a restaurant when I found this little bistro.
tip: 'Chercher' already includes 'for': 'je cherchais un restaurant' = I was looking for a restaurant. Never add 'pour' after it.

target: Je voulais acheter un gâteau mais la boulangerie a fermé.
english: I wanted to buy a cake but the bakery closed.
tip: 'Voulais' is the ongoing wish (I wanted to), 'a fermé' the one event that killed it – passé composé for what suddenly happened.

target: Elles ont adoré le spectacle.
english: They loved the show.
tip: With avoir, the past participle ignores the subject – 'Elles ont adoré' stays adoré, never 'adorées', even for an all-female crowd.

target: Tu réponds à mon message.
english: You reply to my message.
tip: 'Répondre à' requires the preposition 'à': 'Il répond au professeur' (He answers the teacher). Don't forget the 'à'.

target: Il est tombé dans l'escalier.
english: He fell down the stairs.
tip: Tomber takes être, not avoir: 'il est tombé' = he fell. Falling counts as a change of place, so it swings to être like aller and venir.

target: J'ai mis mes chaussures neuves.
english: I put on my new shoes.
tip: Neuf means brand-new, never used: 'chaussures neuves' are fresh out of the box. Nouveau just means new-to-you, so a used car can be 'ma nouvelle voiture'.

target: Il a pris congé vendredi.
english: He took leave on Friday.
tip: No word for 'on' with days: 'vendredi' alone means on Friday. Add le – le vendredi – and it flips to every Friday.

target: Il a travaillé toute la journée.
english: He worked all day.
tip: 'Toute la journée' = all day. 'Tout' agrees with the noun: tout le temps, toute la nuit.

target: Il a dit quelque chose d'intéressant.
english: He said something interesting.
tip: After quelque chose, an adjective needs de: 'quelque chose d'intéressant' = something interesting. Same with rien and quelqu'un: rien de bon.

target: Tu as réussi ton examen ?
english: Did you pass your exam?
tip: To pass an exam is 'réussir un examen' – literally to succeed it. Réussir usually needs à, but with a test it goes direct: 'réussi ton examen'.

target: J'ai appuyé sur le mauvais bouton.
english: I pressed the wrong button.
tip: Appuyer needs sur to mean press: 'appuyer sur le bouton'. You press on the button, not the button itself.

target: Elles ont travaillé dur pour réussir.
english: They worked hard to succeed.
tip: 'Travailler dur' uses the bare adjective dur as its adverb, not durement. A handful of verbs do this: parler fort, coûter cher.

target: J'ai commencé à apprendre la guitare.
english: I started learning the guitar.
tip: Commencer links to a following verb with à: 'commencé à apprendre'. The preposition is fixed – you memorize à vs de per verb.

target: Il a dit qu'il était désolé.
english: He said he was sorry.
tip: Reported speech shifts the tense back: 'il a dit qu'il était désolé' = he said he was sorry. The imparfait était stands in for a present 'je suis désolé'.

target: Elle préférait le chocolat au café.
english: She preferred chocolate over coffee.
tip: Prefer one thing to another with à: 'le chocolat au café' (au = à + le). French says preferred-to, never preferred-than.

target: Nous avons visité le musée dimanche.
english: We visited the museum on Sunday.
tip: 'Visiter' is for places: visiter un musée. For people, use 'rendre visite à': rendre visite à un ami.

target: Elle a promis de revenir bientôt.
english: She promised to come back soon.
tip: Promettre attaches a following verb with de: 'promis de revenir'. Compare commencer à – there's no logic, each verb just picks à or de.
